overview: AutoGroomer sends scripted harassment chat: every 60 ticks it broadcasts a message picked from a fixed pool of 16 hardcoded lines, or with DM Messages enabled it sends /msg <name> <message> to every non-bot, visible player within 8 blocks (distance squared < 64) - once per player per world, or repeatedly every 20 ticks in Spam mode. The Chat Bypass toggle interleaves a random symbol from a five-symbol set after every character to defeat text filters. All traffic goes out as C01PacketChatMessage through the NetHandler's direct queue, and a per-world entity-id list keeps targets from being re-messaged until a world change or module toggle clears it.

sections.p: onPreMotion runs the whole module. With DM Messages off, it sends one public chat message every 60 ticks (ticksExisted % 60 == 0) and returns. With DM Messages on, it iterates mc.theWorld.playerEntities and targets every player that is not the local player, not invisible, not registered in AntiBot.bots, and within 64 squared distance; each target receives a C01PacketChatMessage built as '/msg ' + name + ' ' + message. The ids list of entity ids gates each player to a single message per world, unless Spam mode is enabled - Spam both drops the dedupe and changes the cadence gate to every 20 ticks.

When Chat Bypass is enabled, the message is rebuilt character by character: each letter is appended followed by a random character drawn from the array '⛍⛌⛗⛟', roughly doubling the message length. The goal is to break substring-based filters that look for the banned phrases inside the fixed message pool - the inserted symbols sit between every letter, so no contiguous banned substring survives. The pool itself is hardcoded (16 lines selected by randomInt), and the same pool is used for both public chat and DMs.

The ids list is the only state. It is cleared on every WorldChangedEvent, on module enable, and on module disable, so a player is eligible to be groomed again after any world change or toggle cycle. Because the module holds no timer of its own and relies entirely on ticksExisted arithmetic, the cadence (60 ticks public, 20 ticks spam) is tied to the client's tick counter and drifts with lag and GUI pauses.

files.label: AutoGroomer.java
files.explanation: The module is fully self-contained in one class. onPreMotion branches between public chat (every 60 ticks) and DM mode (per-player /msg within 64 squared distance, deduped by the ids list, re-armed every 20 ticks in Spam mode), builds the bypass-obfuscated message when Chat Bypass is on, and pushes C01PacketChatMessage packets through addToSendQueue. onWorldChanged, onEnable and onDisable all clear the ids list so targets become eligible again.

countering.label: Text (chat frequency and repeat similarity)
countering.explanation: NCP's Text check scores every chat message into data.chatFrequency and data.chatShortTermFrequency (frequency buckets over a sliding window) and adds weighted penalties when a message repeats the player's own recent message (textMsgRepeatSelf), matches a globally recent message (textMsgRepeatGlobal), or arrives too soon after joining or with no movement (textMsgAfterJoin, textMsgNoMoving), all within an 8-second timeout. AutoGroomer cycles a fixed pool of 16 identical lines, so repeat-similarity fires as soon as the pool loops within the timeout window, and Spam or DM mode bursts several C01s inside one tick, blowing past the short-term frequency level. The score is multiplied by a time weight and feeds the standard violation/action pipeline, so sustained grooming accumulates VL even at the slow 60-tick cadence.

countering.label: Commands (command rate)
countering.explanation: Every DM AutoGroomer sends is a command (/msg ...), so it flows through NCP's Commands check, which scores commands per second in data.commandsShortTermWeight and compares against cc.commandsShortTermLevel (violation = max(nw - commandsLevel, shortTermWeight - shortTermLevel)). DM mode iterates all nearby players in a single onPreMotion and queues a /msg for each, so a lobby full of targets produces a burst of commands in the same tick - the exact short-term spike the check is built to catch. Even the public-chat mode is unaffected, but any server running Commands with default levels kills the DM variant within one burst.

countering.label: Captcha (auto-armed chat gate)
countering.explanation: NCP's Captcha check arms a chat gate on suspicion: the player must answer a server-generated question before chat is allowed again, and a wrong or missing answer repeats the question and raises the violation. AutoGroomer has no captcha logic at all - it answers whatever it was about to send, which is never the captcha answer - so the moment any other check (Text frequency, Commands rate) arms the gate, every subsequent groomed message becomes a captcha failure. The module cannot self-recover because it cannot parse the question prompt it receives on S02PacketChat.

countering.label: LetterEngine (obfuscation character analysis)
countering.explanation: LetterEngine is the consistency engine behind NCP's chat analysis: it maintains a per-player character frequency model and evaluates each incoming message's letter distribution for anomalies, configured with threshold weights for letter and character usage. AutoGroomer's Chat Bypass interleaves a fixed five-symbol set ('⛍⛌⛗⛟') after every letter, which doubles message length and produces a perfectly regular letter-symbol-letter-symbol alternation - a character distribution no human typing produces. Because the same pool of lines cycles repeatedly, the per-player frequency model sees the same anomalous composition again and again, pushing the consistency score steadily up and making the bypass worse than useless on NCP servers running the engine.
